d: About the Role the Senior Accountant (reporting to the Finance Manager within the Finance Division) is responsible for analyzing all financial activities, ensuring compliance with accounting, tax, and legal requirements, and preparing budgets and financial reports.
q: Bachelor’s degree in finance or accounting.
Minimum of 5–8 years of relevant accounting experience.
SOCPA certification (mandatory for candidates hired from within Saudi Arabia).
Working knowledge of local tax laws (including ZATCA/VAT regulations), IFRS, and GAAP norms.
Strong financial analysis, budgeting, and project costing skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
Strong written and verbal communication, organizational, and stress management skills.
Ability to train and manage staff, as well as work independently with minimal supervision.
Core and functional competencies including analytical thinking, planning and organizing, influencing and negotiating, integrity, accountability, and cross-functional relationship building.
Familiarity with catering or food industry will be privilege
r: li
Financial Reporting & Statements: Prepare monthly financial reports (balance sheets, profit and loss statements, cash flows) and summarize current and projected financial positions.
li

General Accounting & Reconciliations: Maintain financial records, prepare journal entries, keep ledgers (assets, liabilities, capital), verify financial transactions, and reconcile accounts including bank statements.
li
Compliance & Tax (ZATCA / VAT): Ensure compliance with accounting standards, tax laws, and IFRS norms; prepare monthly VAT returns and verify that customer invoices comply with ZATCA requirements.
li

Budgeting & Forecasting: Prepare budgets and financial forecasts by analyzing past and present operations, costs, trends, and revenues; assist the AR team with collection forecasts and daily/weekly/monthly cashflow improvements.
li
Accounts Payable & Receivable: Verify and approve vendor and customer invoices for payment processing and manage project costing.
li

Month-End Closing & Audits: Check accruals and provisions on closing dates for accurate posting, adhere to the reporting calendar by collecting cross-departmental data (Operations, Logistics, HR, etc.), and liaise with external auditors and consultants.
li

Internal Controls & Stakeholder Relations: Evaluate internal management systems and risks, maintain accounting controls/policies, and build effective relationships with internal teams (Factory, Design & Engineering, Estimation, Supply Chain, HR) and external financial/government entities.
